title: Simple harmonic motion: definition and graphs; Mass–spring and pendulum; Energy in SHM
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 1 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: O01-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; O01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; O03-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; O03-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: O01-1#N.11, O02-1#N.4b, O03-1#N.1b, O03-1#N.9b.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Amplitude
items.clue: Maximum displacement of an oscillating object.

items.label: Restoring force
items.clue: Always points back to equilibrium, opposite to the displacement.

items.label: Turning point
items.clue: Either extreme, x = +A or x = –A, where the oscillator is momentarily at rest.

items.label: Total energy
items.clue: Sum that stays constant for an undamped oscillator: a horizontal line against x.

questions.stem: A pendulum bob swings to and fro in a small arc. At the lowest point of its swing, what are its acceleration along its path and its speed?

options.text: Acceleration along the path greatest; speed zero.
Acceleration along the path zero; speed greatest.
Acceleration along the path zero; speed also zero.
Acceleration along the path greatest; speed greatest.

questions.explanation: The lowest point is equilibrium: the restoring force along the path is zero there. The bob sped up all the way down and starts to slow on the way up, so its speed is greatest here.

questions.stem: A block attached to an ideal spring oscillates on a horizontal surface with negligible friction, with period T. The block is replaced by a block with 4 times the mass, and the new block is set oscillating with 3 times the original amplitude. The new period is how many times T?

A block attached to a horizontal ideal spring oscillates on a surface with negligible friction. At an instant when the block's kinetic energy has its minimum value, which of the following is true of the spring potential energy U_s of the block–spring system?

options.text: It is zero, because the block is momentarily at rest.
It has its maximum value, equal to the system's total energy.
It has its minimum value, as the system then has the least energy.
It has the same value as at every other instant of the motion.

questions.stem: A block of mass m attached to an ideal spring of spring constant k oscillates with amplitude A on a horizontal surface with negligible friction. Which expression gives the speed of the block when it is at x = A/2, halfway between the equilibrium position and a turning point?
